elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate
elements.evidence: "M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement to an Affiliate of Customer"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or pursuant to a merger, acquisition, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assets, stock or securities of Customer"

elements.element: Customer's affiliate/successor assignment right not conditioned on financial qualification of the assignee
elements.evidence: the "$100,000,000" capital-and-surplus condition was deleted; only "so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with" remains

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld)
elements.evidence: "(b) M&I may freely assign this Agreement (i) in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities, or (ii) to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: no competitor restriction anywhere; M&I may assign "to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division of M&I"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "If a Change in Control occurs with respect to Customer, M&I agrees to continue to provide Services under this Agreement" — no termination right conferred

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Customer carve-out for "merger, acquisition, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assets"; M&I "may freely assign ... in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale"
no notice obligation appears; clause only recites "so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: The edit achieves the Customer-side half of the preferred position (affiliate plus merger/acquisition/asset-sale carve-out, with the $100,000,000 qualification removed) but leaves the Vendor-side half untouched: M&I still 'may freely assign' on its own merger, reorganisation or asset sale, so the required Vendor-consent gate (consent not unreasonably withheld) is absent.
The preferred prohibition on assignment to a Customer competitor is nowhere in the operative text; it is also not mentioned in the margin comment.

Fallback is not literally complete either, because no written notice of a successor assignment is required of either party; substantively, however, mutuality and the reasonable-consent standard for other assignments are present.

No Vendor termination right arises on Customer's change of control, so that preferred element is satisfied; the accounts/items volume limits in Section B are untouched commercial terms and are not part of this rule.

Minimality and intent are satisfied: a single targeted replacement of clause (a), preserving the Section 21.11 conditions and all surrounding language, with no new undefined terms or dangling mechanics.
